point: Put an adverb between be and the past participle.
be 動詞和過去分詞之間放副詞。
why: The blank sits between were and calculated. It describes how the charges were calculated, so it needs an adverb: automatically.
空格在 were 和 calculated 之間，說明運費是「怎麼」被計算的，要用副詞 automatically。

gloss.ex: The shipping charge is added at checkout.
Please send the invoice by Friday.
Our billing software sends reminders automatically.

point: seem + adjective.
seem + 形容詞。
why: Seem links the subject to a description. The subject is The terms of the new rental agreement, and the blank says what they seem like. It needs an adjective: acceptable.
seem 把主詞和描述連起來。主詞是 The terms of the new rental agreement，空格說明條款看起來如何，要用形容詞 acceptable。

gloss.ex: Please read the terms before you sign.
The rental agreement lasts one year.
Both parties agreed to the price.

point: After the and before of: a noun.
the 之後、of 之前：用名詞。
why: The blank comes after The and before of the Tamsin Road factory. Together they are the subject of will create, so the blank must be a noun: expansion.
空格在 The 之後、of the Tamsin Road factory 之前，整組是 will create 的主詞，所以要用名詞 expansion。

gloss.ex: Sales grew fast in the northern region.
The new store will create fifty jobs.

point: who refers to a person: use a person noun.
who 指人：用表示人的名詞。
why: The blank is a noun, and who visited the plant and recommended describe a person. A person who checks safety is an inspector.
空格要放名詞，who visited the plant 和 recommended 描述的是人。檢查安全的人是 inspector。

gloss.ex: The plant employs about 300 workers.
The doctor recommended more rest.
We are replacing the old printers.

point: very + adjective + noun.
very + 形容詞 + 名詞。
why: The blank is between very and the noun shutdown, so it must be an adjective. Costly ends in -ly, but it is an adjective meaning "expensive".
空格在 very 和名詞 shutdown 之間，要用形容詞。costly 雖然以 -ly 結尾，但是形容詞，意思是「代價高的」。

gloss.ex: The shutdown lasted two days.
Worn parts can cause machine failures.
The old pump failed last week.

point: An adverb modifies an adjective.
副詞修飾形容詞。
why: The blank is right before the adjective easier. It tells how much easier things are, so it needs an adverb: dramatically.
空格就在形容詞 easier 前面，說明「容易多少」，所以要用副詞 dramatically。

gloss.ex: The booking system shows free rooms.
Please reserve a table for six.
We can travel on short notice.

point: A past time: past tense. No object: passive.
過去的時間用過去式；沒有受詞用被動。
why: Shortly before the building was sold is a fixed time in the past, so the verb is past tense. The cameras did not replace anything; they were replaced.
Shortly before the building was sold 是明確的過去時間，動詞用過去式。攝影機是被換的，所以用 were replaced。

gloss.ex: The security camera covers the front door.
The parking garage closes at midnight.
The laptop is still under warranty.

point: Currently + an action in progress: present continuous.
currently + 正在進行的動作：現在進行式。
why: Currently means now. The technicians have not finished finding the cause of this morning's network outage, so the action is in progress: are investigating.
Currently 指現在。技術人員還沒查出 the cause of this morning's network outage，動作正在進行，所以用 are investigating。

gloss.ex: A technician will visit the office today.
The network outage lasted an hour.

point: After once: present tense for the future.
once 子句：用現在式表示未來。
why: Once starts a time clause, and the main clause says will send, which is future. A time clause uses present tense for a future action: completes.
Once 引導時間子句，主句 will send 是未來。時間子句用現在式表示未來的動作：completes。

gloss.ex: The legal team checks every contract.
The review took about two weeks.
Please sign the revised contract today.

point: since + a point in time: present perfect.
since + 時間點：現在完成式。
why: Since the spring of 2021 starts in the past and runs up to now. The verb must be present perfect: has expanded.
since the spring of 2021 從過去開始、延續到現在，動詞要用現在完成式 has expanded。

gloss.ex: Our delivery network covers the whole island.
We have worked here since the spring.

point: By the time + past: past perfect.
by the time + 過去式：過去完成式。
why: By the time the renovation … was completed in May is a past point. The spending was done before then, so the main clause uses past perfect: had spent.
By the time … was completed in May 是過去的某個時間點。花錢發生在那之前，主句用過去完成式 had spent。

gloss.ex: The renovation will take three months.
Guests wait in the lobby.
The owner of the shop lives nearby.

point: A noun phrase needs a preposition.
名詞片語前要用介系詞。
why: the growing number of attendees is a noun phrase, with no subject and verb. It gives the reason for the move, so use because of.
the growing number of attendees 是名詞片語，沒有主詞和動詞。它是搬會議室的原因，所以用 because of。

gloss.ex: Each attendee gets a name badge.
The conference room seats twenty people.
A growing team needs more space.

point: A full clause needs a conjunction.
完整子句前要用連接詞。
why: they are on the construction site has a subject and a verb, so it is a clause. A conjunction must join it to the main sentence: while.
they are on the construction site 有主詞和動詞，是子句，要用連接詞連到主句：while。

gloss.ex: Workers must wear a hard hat here.
Keep your badge with you at all times.
The construction site is closed on Sundays.

point: A contrast between two sentences: However.
前後兩句轉折：用 However。
why: The first sentence says the supplier charges more. The second says we have decided to keep ordering. The two ideas go against each other, so use However.
第一句說供應商收費較高，第二句說我們決定繼續訂貨。兩句意思相反，所以用 However。

gloss.ex: Our supplier ships every Tuesday.
Our competitors lowered their prices.
We keep spare parts in the store room.

point: unless = except if.
unless = 除非。
why: The rule is that orders after 3 p.m. ship the next day. Paying extra for same-day shipping is an exception to it, so use unless.
規則是下午三點後的訂單隔天出貨。加價選 same-day shipping 是這條規則的例外，所以用 unless。

gloss.ex: Refunds take five business days.
Same-day shipping costs ten dollars more.
You must pay extra for large bags.

point: even though + clause: a contrast.
even though + 子句：表示讓步。
why: A clause follows the blank. Spending far less on advertising would lead you to expect weak sales, but sales still rose. Use Even though.
空格後面是子句。廣告費少很多，照理銷量會差，但銷量 still rose，所以用 Even though。

gloss.ex: Advertising costs rose last year.
This desk lamp has a built-in charger.
Prices may rise by five percent.

point: by = no later than.
by = 最晚在……之前。
why: April 5 is the last day, and must be submitted is a one-time action. It has to be done no later than that date: by.
April 5 是最後一天，must be submitted 是一次性的動作，最晚要在這天之前完成：by。

gloss.ex: Each expense claim needs a receipt.
The first-quarter results look strong.
Please submit the form online.

point: for + a length of time.
for + 一段時間的長度。
why: three days is a length of time. It says how long the entrance will stay closed, so use for.
three days 是一段時間的長度，說明正門要關多久，所以用 for。

gloss.ex: Use the main entrance after 8 a.m.
The floor tiles are made of stone.
The team installed new lights today.

point: upon + noun = as soon as.
upon + 名詞 = 一……就。
why: The certificate is given the moment the course ends. Upon completion of the training course means "as soon as it is completed".
證書在課程結束的當下發給學員。Upon completion of the training course 的意思是「一完成就」。

gloss.ex: Completion of the project is due in May.
Each participant gets a free lunch.
The certificate is signed by the director.

point: since + a past point, with present perfect.
since + 過去時間點，搭配現在完成式。
why: The main verb is has doubled, present perfect. It covers the time from the merger with Kessling Freight last year until now, so the starting point needs Since.
主要動詞是現在完成式 has doubled，涵蓋從 the merger with Kessling Freight last year 到現在，起點要用 Since。

gloss.ex: The merger created a much larger firm.
The company owns a fleet of ten trucks.
Sales doubled in two years.

point: Before a noun, a passive participle takes -ed.
名詞前的被動分詞用 -ed。
why: The price list is something that gets updated. Before the noun price list, a passive meaning takes -ed: updated.
價目表是被更新的東西。在名詞 price list 前面表示被動，用 -ed：updated。

gloss.ex: The price list changes every spring.
You can download the manual here.

point: After a noun, an active participle takes -ing.
名詞後的主動分詞用 -ing。
why: The verb of the sentence is will be listed, so the blank only describes Companies. The companies take part themselves, so the meaning is active: participating.
句子的動詞是 will be listed，空格只是修飾 Companies。公司是自己參加，意思是主動，用 participating。

gloss.ex: We will have a stand at the trade fair.
The catalog lists all our products.
Your name will be listed on the website.

point: The subject receives the action: use -ed.
主詞承受動作：用 -ed。
why: The opening phrase describes the new distribution center. The center did not build anything; it was built in only six months. So use Built.
句首片語描述的是 the new distribution center。物流中心不是自己蓋，而是 in only six months 被蓋好，所以用 Built。

gloss.ex: The distribution center ships to every state.
We can process refunds within two days.
We received fifty orders this morning.

point: A thing that causes the feeling takes -ing.
造成感受的事物用 -ing。
why: The subject is the sales figures. The figures cause disappointment in people; they do not feel it. So use disappointing.
主詞是 the sales figures。數字是讓人失望的事物，自己不會感到失望，所以用 disappointing。

gloss.ex: The sales figures will be released on Monday.
Kitchen appliances are on sale this week.
The board meets every quarter.

point: An adverb modifies a verb.
副詞修飾動詞。
why: find the Pembry Conference Center is already a full clause. The blank says how visitors find it, so it modifies the verb and needs an adverb: easily.
find the Pembry Conference Center 已經是完整的子句。空格說明訪客怎麼找到，修飾動詞，要用副詞 easily。

gloss.ex: The signs point to the exit.
Calling ahead saves time at the door.
Can you give me directions to the station?

point: A sentence needs a main verb.
句子需要一個主要動詞。
why: The subject is The results, and it has no main verb yet. The blank must be that verb. Results is plural, so use indicate.
主詞是 The results，還沒有主要動詞，空格就要填這個動詞。results 是複數，所以用 indicate。

gloss.ex: The customer survey takes five minutes.
Costs rose slightly in May.
Delivery usually takes two days.

point: A future point, counting up to it: will have been.
累積到未來某個時間點：will have been。
why: when she retires at the end of next month is a point in the future. By then she will have completed thirty-two years, so use will have been.
when she retires at the end of next month 是未來的時間點。到那時她會已經待滿 thirty-two years，所以用 will have been。

gloss.ex: A junior engineer works under a senior lead.
She works for a law firm.
He retires next June.

point: provided that = only if.
provided that = 只要、前提是。
why: The dock has no staff after 5 p.m. The warehouse takes deliveries then only if the driver has arranged access … in advance. That is a condition, so use provided that.
碼頭五點後沒人值班。只有司機 has arranged access … in advance 才收貨，這是條件，所以用 provided that。

gloss.ex: Trucks park at the loading dock.
The night supervisor locks the gate.
Please book your seat in advance.

point: After a noun, a passive participle takes -ed.
名詞後的被動分詞用 -ed。
why: The verb of the sentence is have recommended, so the blank only describes The consultants. They were brought in by the company, so the meaning is passive: hired.
句子的動詞是 have recommended，空格只是修飾 The consultants。顧問是被公司請來的，意思是被動，用 hired。

gloss.ex: The consultant reviewed our budget.
Operations are managed from the head office.
We have a regional office in Taipei.

point: in accordance with = following a rule.
in accordance with = 依照（規定）。
why: The chemicals must be labeled and stored as the guidelines set out in section 4 say. Following a rule is in accordance with.
化學品要照 the guidelines set out in section 4 的規定來標示和存放。遵照規定就是 in accordance with。

gloss.ex: Some chemicals must be kept cold.
Please label each box clearly.
The rules are set out in the contract.

point: attribute A to B.
attribute A to B（把 A 歸因於 B）。
why: The verb is attributes. Its pattern is attribute A to B. Here A is most of the drop in second-quarter shipments, and B is delays at the Port of Castrell.
動詞是 attributes，句型是 attribute A to B。A 是 most of the drop in second-quarter shipments，B 是 delays at the Port of Castrell。

gloss.ex: She attributes the growth to better training.
Shipments fell by ten percent in March.
The logistics manager plans all deliveries.

point: on behalf of = representing.
on behalf of = 代表。
why: The writer is inviting you to our annual awards dinner, so the writer speaks for the association. Speaking for a group is on behalf of.
寫信的人邀請你參加 our annual awards dinner，寫信的人是替協會發言。代表團體說話就是 on behalf of。

gloss.ex: We invite you to our open house.
The Association holds a meeting each May.
The awards dinner starts at seven.
